excerpt_i18n.en:
From August 15 to 21, 2026, the 35th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2026) will be held in Bremen, Germany's "City of Space." As the top-tier event in AI with the longest history and the strongest emphasis on theoretical depth, IJCAI is seen by many practitioners as synonymous with "System 2" (slow thinking). But in 2026, this academic gathering in Europe is closely capturing the attention of China's industry across the ocean, driven by a set of special signals. This is the first "big test" after CCF (China Computer Federation) downgraded its rating, and a crossroads where large language models (LLMs) are shifting from a "parameter race" to a "logic offensive." As the brute-force aesthetics of Scaling Law begin to hit diminishing returns, Chinese tech giants are trying to find the theoretical key to solving LLM "hallucination" and "robustness" issues in Bremen. The reporting teams from Leiphone and AI Technology Review will fly to Germany to uncover the intertwined landscape of academia and industry.

01 The First Year After the Rating Downgrade: Indicators Cool Down, "Rigid Demand" Heats Up
